fixes.explanation: Fire it is. The text says fire from the LORD blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp. That came after He heard their complaining and His anger was kindled. Imagine pulling a tray and the edges are the first thing to go. That's the outskirts, friend.

Sinai is a real place on Israel's journey (Exodus 19:1), so I see why it came to mind. But the people say they remember the fish they ate freely in Egypt. Their list goes on with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic. Sinai isn't on that menu.
That's what he says to the LORD. Moses asks, “…please kill me right now…” I think this one hurts, friend. He says it right after telling the LORD the burden of all these people is too much for him.

False is right. The Spirit rested on the seventy elders and they prophesied, and the text says they never did so again. So it happened that one time. Think of a batch that comes out once and the recipe never works the same again, friend.

Craved. The text says they called the place Kibroth-hattaavah, “…because there they buried the people who had craved other food.” The name records that people were buried there. I think this one is heavy, friend, and the name keeps the craving in front of us.
